summary: Duke meets 100% of demonstrated need for the international students it admits. Its Karsh International Scholarship goes further, covering the full cost of attendance plus three summers of funded research or internships.
covers: Aid meeting the full demonstrated need of admitted international students.
The Karsh International Scholarship covers tuition, room, board and mandatory fees, plus any demonstrated need beyond those costs.
Karsh Scholars also receive funding for three summers of research, unpaid internships or other opportunities.
eligibility: International first-year applicants who apply for financial aid and have demonstrated need (a requirement for Karsh).
You must not already hold a bachelor's degree.
Duke considers international students' financial need in admission (it is need-aware for them), so a strong application matters even more.
how_to_apply: Apply to Duke through the Common Application or QuestBridge.
Tick the financial aid interest box and submit the CSS Profile — there is no separate Karsh application.
Choose binding Early Decision (2 November) or Regular Decision (4 January).
Karsh finalists are identified from the admission and aid files.
watch_out: Asking for aid can affect an international applicant's chances at Duke — unlike at need-blind colleges.
Karsh is highly selective; most aided international students receive need-based aid instead.

faq.q: What if I don't ask for aid when I apply?
faq.a: Then you can never get Duke aid. International students admitted without ticking the financial aid interest box are ineligible for aid for all their undergraduate years.

faq.q: Do I have to reapply for aid every year?
faq.a: No. Duke gives international students four-year aid awards, which renew automatically once your first-year award is complete.

faq.q: Do I need the SAT, ACT or an English test?
faq.a: No. Duke is test-optional in the 2026–27 cycle, including for merit scholarship consideration, and English tests are recommended rather than required.
